messages.author: 4a3bb16308e8b045
messages.subject: What does check="start" do?
parts:
Dear all,

unfortunately, I Google and searching the archives of this list didn't answer the following question regarding the check="start" option for cfa() in lavaan.

I have fitted a complex CFA model using lavaan (a multistate-multitrait model of six item-specific traits at two time points), which yields nonpositive definiteness ("WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite"). When I include check="start" in the options, this warning no longer shows, but I'm not quite sure a) what this option does; b) whether this means that the original problem has been resolved (or that merely the warning message has disappeared). If somebody could explain the option or point me to a relevant source, I'd be grateful for that.

Reproducible example:
library(lavaan)
model <- readLines(url("https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/66464491/model.txt"))
data <- read.table(url('https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/66464491/msmt-data.csv'))
fit <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml") # warning: nonpositive definite
fit1 <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml", check="start") # no warning

Kind regards,
Simon

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: What does check="start" do?
parts: I Google and searching the archives of this list didn't answer the following question regarding the check="start" option for cfa() in lavaan.
You can see what the argument does on the options help page: ?lavaan::lavOptions
When I include check="start" in the options, this warning no longer shows

Ah, I was surprised by that as well, since this detail is not in the help page.  I'm not even sure it was intentional, but when you request a check, it appears that the warnings are not automatically displayed.  They are, however, still there. 

> warnings()
> fit1 <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml", check="start")

> warnings()
Warning messages:
1: closing unused connection 3 (https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/66464491/model.txt)
2: In lav_object_post_check(object) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables
                is not positive definite;
                use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

And you can tell the results are the same by print some results from both fit and fit1.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: What does check="start" do?
parts: > fit <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml") # warning: nonpositive definite

The default value for 'check' is:

> lavOptions()$check
[1] "start" "post"

So -by default- both the starting values are checked, and the
post-estimated statistics (ie model implied ov/lv covariances). It is
the latter one that triggers the warning about the nonpositive lv
covariance matrix.

If you specify check="start", you only request "check the starting
values", but not the model-implied ov/lv covariances. Therefore, no warning.

This will trigger the warning again:

fit1 <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml", check="post")

Yves.

> fit1 <- cfa(model, data=data, missing="fiml", check="start") # no warning
>
> Kind regards,
> Simon
